description: We are now welcoming members who are interested in joining “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” Be part of an exciting initiative exploring how NASA data can help transform and adapt modern agriculture!
summary: FIELD SHIFT is a web app that turns free NASA satellite data into a simple crop-health picture for small farms. A farmer saves a field, and the app requests its vegetation history from NASA's MODIS MOD13Q1 product through NASA AppEEARS. It then shows NDVI and EVI scores, valid-pixel and coverage figures, a field map, a time-series chart, plain-language recommendations and a one-page PDF report. By making a reading that arrives every 16 days as easy to read as a weather forecast, FIELD SHIFT helps farmers, starting with paddy growers in Kerala, catch a decline early and adapt water, nutrients and timing as the season unfolds.
details:
FIELD SHIFT turns free NASA satellite data into a simple field health picture for small farms. A user saves a field once, requests its vegetation history from NASA, and reads four numbers (mean NDVI, mean EVI, valid pixels and coverage), a boundary map, a time-series chart and a short recommendation with the evidence behind it. Nothing is guessed or simulated: every reading comes from NASA’s MODIS MOD13Q1 vegetation product (250 m, one reading per 16 days), retrieved through NASA AppEEARS.

How it works: The user chooses a farm and date range. FIELD SHIFT files an AppEEARS request, and NASA cuts out only that field from the satellite product. FIELD SHIFT then averages the usable pixels for each date, and the dashboard, recommendations and a PDF report update themselves. A request usually takes 5 to 45 minutes and keeps running on the server if the user closes the page. Users can upload a GeoJSON or KML boundary, or measure a single pixel at the farm’s centre.

Benefits and intended impact: It was built for paddy fields in Kerala, where plots are small, monsoon cloud hides the ground for weeks, and extension officers cannot visit every field. It supports adaptive farming by letting farmers do five things:

  • catch a decline early
  • tell a bad week from a bad season
  • save fertiliser and spraying on healthy fields
  • avoid mistaking a nutrient or pest problem for a water shortage
  • keep a dated record to compare seasons

Distant and tiny plots still get measured every 16 days, at no cost. The same method works for any crop wherever MODIS covers.

Tools and technology: NASA MODIS (Terra), the MOD13Q1 product, NASA AppEEARS and NASA Earthdata Login, with data courtesy of NASA LP DAAC. [Add your frontend, backend, language and hosting here, e.g. HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Python, hosting platform.] NASA credentials are stored on the server only, so the browser never sees them.

Creativity: Instead of showing raw satellite indices, FIELD SHIFT translates them into plain-language advice. Every technical term in the app links to a glossary written for farmers, and each recommendation shows its supporting numbers so the advice can be checked.

Factors considered: The satellite pixel is about 6 hectares, so a small field is averaged with its surroundings. Monsoon cloud leaves gaps, so the app reports valid pixels and coverage and warns when coverage is below about 50%. A pixel quality filter lets users trade reliability against the number of dates. The app is also honest that it is one input, not a verdict, and should be combined with what the farmer sees in the field.
